newsitem.title: UK: Clarke - UK GDP growth more than 3.0% next year.
newsitem.headline: Clarke - UK GDP growth more than 3.0% next year.

text.p: Britain's economy will achieve growth of more than three percent next year, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday. "It's obviously on course for over three percent growth next year," he said on BBC radio.
He said his decision to raise interest rates would have no impact on his November 26 budget.

"It's got nothing to do with the budget," Clarke said. "The budget is there to look after public finances. I'm going to set a budget that will keep us on course for a balanced budget over the medium-term."

Clarke also said he was confident the government's target of 2.5 percent for underlying inflation would be met. Retail prices excluding mortgage interest rates edged up to 2.9 percent year-on-year in September.
"I'm confident we will meet it," he said.
